india.one_line: Today, Indian IT firms focus on AI monetisation, expand partnerships, strengthen AI talent, and secure disease surveillance funding.

themes.title: Low-capital IT firms gain advantage
themes.text: According to an Anand Rathi report, IT companies capable of monetising enterprise AI without substantial capital investments may gain an advantage. Investors are increasingly differentiating between businesses funding AI infrastructure and those generating returns from its adoption.

stories.headline: IT firms with lower capital requirements may gain as investors shift focus to AI monetisation: Report

themes.title: Enterprise AI partnerships expand
themes.text: Global Capability Centres and Indian IT services firms are forming partnerships to deploy enterprise AI and integrate solutions across large organizations. A new study by ANSR and HFS Research scored India's GCC ecosystem at 61.9, noting that 83% of GCCs are mission‑critical while only 17% have full budget authority.

stories.headline: India's GCCs and IT firms form enterprise AI partnerships

themes.title: AI workforce and leadership strengthen
themes.text: Cognizant has formed a Claude Frontier Capability Group with 25,000 professionals to deliver Anthropic's AI assistant, training or certifying over 44,000 associates. Sarvam AI appointed former Google Cloud India Managing Director Sashikumar Sreedharan as President and Chief Business Officer, bringing decades of technology experience.

stories.headline: Cognizant forms Claude Frontier Capability Group with 25,000 staff
Sarvam AI appoints ex-Google Cloud India MD Sashikumar Sreedharan as President and CBO
